newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary futures exchange to vote on bourse merger.
newsitem.headline: Hungary futures exchange to vote on bourse merger.

text.p: The Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) expects to vote on a possible merger with the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) at a meeting later this month, the BCE's chairman said on Thursday.
BCE board chairman Szergej Keresztesi told Reuters that members of the BCE would vote on a proposal to merge with the bourse at a general membership meeting on November 27.

"Today's situation now is targeted towards cooperation between the two exchanges and the BCE wants to create the most optimum situation with optimum treatment for members of the BCE on the securities market.
"The stock exchange looks very much supportive. What's more they were also suggesting the preparation of a declaration that the two exchanges should merge," Keresztesi said in an interview.

The BCE trades in futures for live hogs, wheat, wheat flour, barley, maize and sunflower seed, as well as for U.S. dollars, German marks, European currency units, Swiss francs, British pounds, Italian lire, Japanese yen and 90-day forint interest rates.
Keresztesi said no government approval for a merger would be necessary if parliament approved a new securities law, passage of which was expected in a matter of days.
BSE officials were not immediately available for comment.
Keresztesi added that the BSE had broached the merger idea in August. "We are just reacting to their proposal."
The BCE has total daily turnover of about 3.0 to 4.0 billion forints ($18.86-$25.14 million) and the 1996 total was expected to be between 800 and 900 billion forints.
The BSE had daily spot share turnover of around one billion forints.
Keresztesi added that by the end of the year the BCE expected the number of traded contracts to exceed six million.
